study_identification.title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

study_characteristics.study_objective: Identify MDD subtypes using individualized deviations in resting-state functional connectivity by comparing each subject's edges to normative ranges derived from healthy controls via tolerance intervals, and evaluate reproducibility and clinical relevance.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests (Bonferroni-corrected) to assess subtype vs HC abnormalities at network/node levels; linear regressions linking extreme connections to symptom severity, illness duration, and age of onset; functional enrichment analysis with Neurosynth terms; classification analyses comparing case-control accuracy using all patients vs subtype-specific models.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Two robust MDD subtypes show opposite-signed, widespread rsFC abnormalities relative to HCs; subtypes markedly improve case-control discriminability and are reproducible across subsampling, leave-one-site-out, parameter changes, and in untreated patients; patterns differ from schizophrenia.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Out of 19,900 edges, 556 showed >95% consistency as extreme in MDD. Subtype 1 exhibited broadly increased connectivity (19,579/19,900 edges), whereas subtype 2 showed broadly decreased connectivity (15,405/19,900). Network-level abnormalities concentrated within/between VN, DMN, FPN, and VAN; node-level peaks included cingulate and striatum (Fig. 2B–C). Cluster significance confirmed (SigClust); stability high via subsampling and LOSO. In untreated patients, case-control accuracy improved (all: 63.01%; subtype 1: 83.05%; subtype 2: 70.39%). Disease-specificity: schizophrenia (COBRE) showed a different edge pattern (notably VN, SMN, VAN).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional design limits stability inference; limited clinical variables restricted further subtype comparisons; unmeasured confounds (smoking/drinking) may influence results; exclusion of comorbidities limits generalizability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: No global signal regression; ComBat harmonization prior to deviation computation; subtype abnormalities assessed controlling for age, sex, site, motion; features linked to reward-related processes via functional enrichment.
